content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., sentiment > 0.75 → forecast too high).
- Underestimate when sentiment is low or flat (sentiment < 0.3 → model underreacts, misses downward momentum).
- Lag in correction: model often delays response to sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment rises sharply — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows; apply smoothing or decay to recent history when sentiment is volatile.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overreact to short-term sentiment; reduce forecast amplitude when sentiment is stable or trending sideways.
- Avoid “sentiment echo”: if sentiment is rising but price is falling, model often ignores divergence — adjust downward if sentiment > 0.75 and price < 0.5% of recent high.
